title: Public initiatives to support entrepreneurs: Credit guarantees versus co-funding
summary_en: Governments can support entrepreneurs in two contrasting ways: guaranteeing the loans private banks make, or directly co-funding the projects with public capital. Arping, Lóránth and Morrison model the trade-off and show that credit guarantees are preferable when the bank screens projects well (the public sector free-rides on bank diligence), while co-funding dominates when banks have limited screening incentive. The paper provides a clean theoretical map for choosing between two policy levers that look interchangeable in practice but generate different equilibrium screening incentives.
data_used: Theoretical paper. No primary dataset; the analysis is a contract-theoretic model of entrepreneur–bank–government interaction.
policy_relevance: Directly relevant to Hungarian SME and start-up support policy (Garantiqa, MFB credit guarantee programmes, Széchenyi Tőkebefektetési Alap, EXIM): the paper provides the analytical case for using guarantees in established lending markets where banks already screen well, and co-funding in earlier-stage segments where screening is weak. Useful for ITM / NGM choice between the Garantiqa-style guarantee mix and direct equity-fund expansion.
